caseStudies.subtitle: 從醫學到迷因的極限漂移
caseStudies.etymology: 源自拉丁語 toxicum（箭毒），最初是非常生硬、嚴格的醫學和化學術語，用來描述物理上的「有毒物質」。
caseStudies.shift: 從「物質中毒」一路漂移到 2000 年代流行歌裡的「情感傷害」（如 Britney Spears 的歌），再到近代社交媒體與職場文化中全面爆發的「Toxic relationship / Toxic productivity」。
caseStudies.linguisticInsight: Metaphorical Extension（隱喻延伸）——展現人類如何把具象的物理威脅，完美借用到抽象的人際心理狀態上。

caseStudies.subtitle: 從「生病」到「讚嘆」的極端反轉
caseStudies.etymology: 古日耳曼語根源，數百年來一直指「身體生病、感到噁心或虛弱」。
caseStudies.shift: 在街頭文化（Hip-hop / 滑板圈）中發生了完全相反的 Amelioration（詞義褒化）。當有人說 "That trick was sick!" 時，意思為「太神了／超帥的」。
caseStudies.linguisticInsight: Subcultural Inversion / Amelioration——次文化刻意用負面詞彙表達至高讚譽，藉此建立內團體（In-group）的認同與排他性。

caseStudies.subtitle: 大腦追求極致效率的產物
caseStudies.etymology: 網路聊天室與社群媒體時代的產物（Be Right Back / Greatest of All Time）。
caseStudies.shift: 將一整句話「壓縮」成一個像發音符號一樣的全新實體，成為數位溝通的通用捷徑。
caseStudies.linguisticInsight: Blending & Acronymization（混成與首字母縮略）——體現大腦對 Cognitive Efficiency（認知與溝通效率）的追求。

quizQuestions.question: Regarding the evolution of 'Toxic' from a medical term to interpersonal relationships, which linguistic explanation is most accurate?
options: A) It occurs because medical vocabulary naturally shortens to satisfy the laziness principle.
B) It is a classic case of Metaphorical Extension, transferring physical venom to abstract psychological harm.
C) It represents a complete semantic inversion known as Amelioration.
D) It is a meaningless spelling error generated randomly by internet memes.
quizQuestions.explanation: Toxic originally denoted physical poison. Through metaphorical extension, our brains mapped this concept onto toxic workplaces and relationships.

quizQuestions.question: In skate culture or hip-hop, saying 'That trick was sick!' exemplifies which linguistic phenomenon?
options: A) Semantic Bleaching: The literal meaning fades completely into a punctuation mark.
B) Clipping: Truncating a long word down to a single syllable.
C) Subcultural Inversion / Amelioration: Deliberately repurposing a negative term to express high praise.
D) Etymological Fallacy: Misunderstanding the original Germanic spelling.
quizQuestions.explanation: Subcultures often invert norms by transforming negative or uncomfortable terms into strong positive praise to establish group identity.

quizQuestions.question: Why do digital natives frequently use acronyms like 'GOAT' or 'BRB'?
options: A) Ancient English spelling rules formally mandated sentence abbreviation.
B) It reflects the pursuit of Cognitive Efficiency, compressing complex structures into high-density symbols.
C) It is an extreme example of complete semantic death.
D) It is an official government standard for faster typing speeds.
quizQuestions.explanation: Under the pressure of real-time messaging, cognitive and social collaboration drives abbreviation to create functional language shortcuts.

pillars.title: 1. Semantic Shift
pillars.definition: The evolution of a word's meaning over time, where the underlying concept undergoes pejoration, amelioration, or complete inversion.

pillars.title: 2. Clipping
pillars.definition: The morphological process of shortening a polysyllabic lexeme without altering its core lexical category or semantic intent.

pillars.title: 3. Borrowing
pillars.definition: The adoption of loanwords from external languages or subcultural lexicons into the primary linguistic framework.

pillars.title: 4. Blending
pillars.definition: The coalescence of two distinct lexemes and their meanings to forge a novel compound concept.
